pictures.scene: Kitty Kielland, Peat Bog on Jæren — the wide empty bog lying silent under a pale sky, a song a Psalm of Asaph, O God be not silent be not speechless
pictures.name: pd_kielland_torvmyr

pictures.scene: Andreas Achenbach, Sturm an der Mole — the sea breaking white over the pier in the gale, be not still O God, see how Your enemies rage
pictures.name: pd_achenbach_mole

pictures.scene: Rosa Bonheur, The Horse Fair — the great horses rearing and tossing their heads in the crowd, how Your foes have reared their heads, with cunning they scheme against Your people
pictures.name: pd_bonheur_marche_chevaux

pictures.scene: Jacques Raymond Brascassat, Le Loup — the wolf come down on the flock in the open field, and conspire against those You cherish, saying come let us erase them as a nation
pictures.name: pd_brascassat_le_loup

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Conspiracy of the Batavians under Claudius Civilis — the swords brought together over one table in the dark, may the name of Israel be remembered no more, for with one mind they plot together
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_civilis

pictures.scene: Francesco Maffei, Joseph Sold by his Brothers — the brothers striking their bargain over one of their own, they form an alliance against You, the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites
pictures.name: pd_maffei_jozef_verkocht

pictures.scene: Charles-Théodore Frère, La Caravane — the camel train crossing the desert out of the east, of Moab and the Hagrites, of Gebal Ammon and Amalek
pictures.name: pd_frere_caravane

pictures.scene: Abraham Storck, Een rivierzicht — the ships of the coast gathered into one water, of Philistia with the people of Tyre, even Assyria has joined them
pictures.name: pd_storck_rivierzicht

pictures.scene: Alexandre-Gabriel Decamps, Marius défait les Cimbres — the whole host thrown forward against the line, lending strength to the sons of Lot
pictures.name: pd_decamps_cimbres

pictures.scene: Gerbrand van den Eeckhout, The Angel and Gideon — Gideon called at the threshing floor before he went out by night, do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon
pictures.name: pd_eeckhout_gideon

pictures.scene: George Clausen, The Plough — the plough left standing in the empty field at nightfall, who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground
pictures.name: pd_clausen_the_plough

pictures.scene: Karl von Piloty, Thusnelda im Triumphzug des Germanicus — the captive chiefs and their bound old king dragged past the throne, make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna
pictures.name: pd_piloty_thusnelda

pictures.scene: Adriaen van de Velde, Arcadisch landschap met rustende herders en vee — the herds lying at ease on the best of the grass, who said let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God
pictures.name: pd_velde_arcadisch

pictures.scene: Eastman Johnson, Winnowing Grain — the grain poured out of the basket so the wind carries the chaff away, make them like tumbleweed O my God, like chaff before the wind
pictures.name: pd_johnson_winnowing

pictures.scene: Alexey Denisov-Uralsky, Waldbrand — the forest burning with its smoke standing up over the hills, as fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze
pictures.name: pd_denisov_waldbrand

pictures.scene: Józef Chełmoński, Thunderstorm — the herd driven in panic and the people bent double as the lightning comes down, so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm
pictures.name: pd_chelmonski_burza

pictures.scene: Francisco Pradilla, La Rendición de Granada — the beaten king riding out with the keys of the city he has lost, cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name O LORD
pictures.name: pd_pradilla_granada

pictures.scene: Lucas van Valckenborch, The Tower of Babel — the huge unfinished tower and the man who ordered it built, may they be ever ashamed and terrified, may they perish in disgrace
pictures.name: pd_valckenborch_babel

pictures.scene: François Diday, Paysage alpestre au lac — the one great mountain standing up alone in the evening gold, may they know that You alone whose name is the LORD
pictures.name: pd_diday_alpestre

pictures.scene: Harald Sohlberg, Winter Night in the Mountains — the snow peaks and the one star standing over the whole still earth, are Most High over all the earth
pictures.name: pd_sohlberg_vinternatt

lines.text: A song. A Psalm of Asaph.
O God, be not silent; be not speechless;
be not still, O God.
See how Your enemies rage,
how Your foes have reared their heads.
With cunning they scheme against Your people
and conspire against those You cherish,
saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation;
may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
For with one mind they plot together;
they form an alliance against You—
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
of Moab and the Hagrites,
of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek,
of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them,
lending strength to the sons of Lot.
Selah
Do to them as You did to Midian,
as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,
who perished at Endor
and became like dung on the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,
and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us possess for ourselves
the pastures of God.”
Make them like tumbleweed, O my God,
like chaff before the wind.
As fire consumes a forest,
as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with Your tempest,
and terrify them with Your storm.
Cover their faces with shame,
that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
May they be ever ashamed and terrified;
may they perish in disgrace.
May they know that You alone,
whose name is the LORD,
are Most High over all the earth.
